## Contract Value is Relevant in the Modern NBA

* New CBA regulations complicate modern roster building
* Good contracts are just as important as on-court talent
* Our question: Which NBA players are on the most valuable contracts?

![](cropped-rocketsmoney_getty_ringer.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Why is this Important?

* Helps us identify trends and types of players to target/avoid
* Increase good contracts that extend championship windows
* Prevent poor contracts that could set franchises back

* To do this, we must build an on-court impact metric and compare it with contract value

## Building a Metric that Matters

* Looking at points or assists doesn't tell the whole story
* Contract Value Index - metric used to compare on court value with salary
    * Win Shares - estimate number of wins a player contributes to their team
    * VORP - measures a player's output compared to a replacement player
    * Salary - total money player made in a season
* Using both win shares and VORP, we can balance individual and team contribution

## Building a Metric that Matters

* Need to use Z-scores to normalize our data
    * Allows for everything to be compared directly
* $CVI = \frac{Z(VORP) + Z(WS)}{2} - Z(Salary)$
* Averaging VORP and win shares balances the two
* Subtracting salary allows us to see difference between production value and contract value
    * Positive = valuable players, negative = non-valuable players

## Clean Data is Good Data

* Pulled data from Basketball Reference (performance) and ESPN (contract) - both from 2024-2025 season
    * Basketball Reference - remove rows with duplicates and missing values, select relevant columns, standardize player names
    * ESPN - fix header, rename and select relevant columns, remove repeated headers, clean player names and salaries

## Clean Data is Good Data

* Merge both datasets on player name and rename columns
* Account for traded players by only keeping the "2TM" entry and removing others with the same player
* Export into final CSV - 467 entries total

![](PlayerTable.png){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## First, Some Exploratory Efficiency Metrics

* In our efficiency metrics, we found that 
    * The WS/48 minutes mean was 0.0915
        * For every 48 minutes played, the average player is responsible for 0.0915 units of a win
    * The VORP/million mean was 0.0462
        * For every million dollars, the average player provides 0.0462 points of value over a replacement

## Detecting Outliers

* We used a QQ plot to analyze VORP/million outliers
* Mostly followed a normal distribution expect for the tails
![Q-Q Plot: Identifying Elite Value](qq_plot_vorp.png){width=70% fig-align="center"}

## K-Clustering

* We used 4 clusters on the data which can be understood as:
    * Superstars - High salary, VORP, and MP
    * Value - High VORP, low salary
    * Overpaid - High salary, low VORP
    * Rotation - Moderate VORP and salary

## K-Clustering Visual

* Some outliers include Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokic, and Giannis Antetokounmpo

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Categories found from top 20

* Tier 1 - Statistical anomalies (Jokic, Gilgeous-Alexander)
    * Despite having massive contracts - their play is so good that they are still the most valuable

![](JokicAlexander.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Tier 2 - Rookie contracts (Sengun, Duren, Williams, Mobley, Thompson, Wagner, Kessler)
    * Players who are significantly outperforming their standard rookie deals and are in line for big extensions

![](DurenMobley.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Tier 3 - Elite value contracts (Zubac, Pritchard, Allen, Kornet, Jerome, Hart, White, Reaves)
    * Most undervalued players in the league
    * Teams recognize their abilities early and sign them to long-term, team-friendly deals

![](HartWhite.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Categories found from bottom 20

* Tier 1 - Unfortunate injury luck (Embiid, Ingram, Leonard, Murray, Middleton, Markannen)
    * Almost all of them missed at least half of the season, and typically are high performers

![](LeonardEmbiid.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Tier 2 - Overvalued contracts (Beal, Kuzma, McCollum, Rozier, Lavine, VanVleet, Vassell, Brown, Durant, Booker)
    * Teams either overpaid, or the player's production dipped after they signed an extension
    * Some of these should be taken with a grain of salt

![](BealKuzma.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Analyzing Significant Results

* Tier 3 - Bad contracts and injuries (George, Ayton, Grant, Brown)
    * Struggle to stay on the court and perform when they are available
    * Teams must avoid these contracts

![](AytonGeorge.jpg){fig-align="center" width=80%}

## Our Results Exemplify Key Takeaways

* Hitting on draft picks is critical
* Teams need to invest early and long-term in elite skillsets from role players
    * Elite shooting, rim protection, perimeter defense, etc.
* Players who consistently get injured are not worth significant investment
* Need to value a player's age and future outlook more than their past production
    * If it isn't worth the money, likely need to seek a trade

## Implementation in Today's NBA

* Teams have access to the needed metrics through ESPN and Basketball Reference
    * VORP, WS, Salary, Games Played, Age, etc.
* When it comes time to negotiate an extension or sign a free agent, front offices can measure different salary levels to see when the price is no longer worth it
* They can also identify traits in their own players that align with those of the most/least valuable contracts to guide their decision-making

## There is Still Room to Grow

* This is only based on one season's data
    * Need a bigger sample to better understand player contracts
* Adding other statistics to our metric could make it more accurate
* Why are players like Jaylen Brown, Devin Booker on bad contracts?
    * Not winning enough games? Plateaued production over time? Other?
